A.summary:
This commit adds sashiko-cli, a new command-line client for talking to a
running Sashiko server over its HTTP API. It also derives Deserialize on the
API and DB response structs (and Serialize on SubmitRequest) so the CLI can
parse server responses and build submit requests. It adds the chrono
dependency and enables clap's "env" feature.

User-visible effect: a new binary, sashiko-cli, with the subcommands submit,
status, list and show. Global options are --server (also read from the
SASHIKO_SERVER environment variable) and --format text|json.

Submit auto-detects the input kind. "-" or a regular file is sent as an
mbox, an argument containing ".." is sent as a range, and anything else is
sent as a single commit. With no input, it reads stdin if piped, otherwise
it uses HEAD. The --type, --repo and --baseline options override the
defaults.

Before:
  There was no dedicated client. Users had to call the REST endpoints
  by hand, for example:
  curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/submit \
       -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
       -d '{"type":"remote","sha":"HEAD","repo":"/path/to/repo"}'
  curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/stats

After:
  sashiko-cli submit HEAD~3..HEAD
  Success: Submission accepted. ID: <id>

  sashiko-cli status
  Server Status:
    Version:   <version>
    Messages:  <n>
    Patchsets: <n>
  Queue Breakdown:
    Pending         <n>
    ...

  sashiko-cli list --per-page 20 pending
  ID     Status     Subject        Date
  <id>   Pending    <subject>      <local time>

  sashiko-cli show latest
  Patchset Details:
    ID, Subject, Author, Status, Date, per-patch status and apply
    errors, plus the review verdict, model and summary if a review
    exists.

Errors are printed as "Error: ..." with a hint (for example, to check that
the server is running), and the process exits with status 1. Passing
--format json prints the raw API data as pretty JSON instead.
A.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_show), the review is fetched
  from /api/review using the patchset id, but get_review in src/api.rs and
  Database::get_review_details in src/db.rs key the lookup on reviews.id.
  The ids come from different tables, so show prints another patchset's
  review under this patchset's header, or none. Take the review id from the
  reviews array in the /api/patch response instead.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_submit), the default input is
  the literal string HEAD, sent as SubmitRequest::Remote sha. submit_patch
  in src/api.rs uses it verbatim as the patchset id, and
  create_fetching_patchset in src/db.rs returns the existing row unless it
  is Failed or Fetching. src/fetcher.rs also never resolves the ref to a
  SHA. Repeat submissions collide on one HEAD@sashiko.local id and are
  silently attached to an old patchset or ignored, while the API still
  answers accepted.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_list), the subject is
  truncated with a byte slice at offset 45 after a byte-length check. If
  that offset falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character the CLI panics and
  the rest of the page is lost. Subjects come from untrusted mail and are
  often non-ASCII. Truncate on a char boundary. The byte-based width
  padding also misaligns non-ASCII text.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_list), the same subject slice
  at byte 45 panics on multi-byte UTF-8 input, violating the error-handling
  guideline on string slicing. This repeats the finding above, reported by
  later review stages, and the same fix applies.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (main), the settings fallback
  Settings::new().unwrap_or_else(|_| Settings::new().expect(...)) retries
  the identical call and then panics. Running outside the server directory
  or with a malformed Settings.toml panics even when --server is given. The
  comment promises defaults that do not exist, and a malformed file should
  fail with a clear error.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_list and handle_show), the
  list filter and the show id are spliced into URLs without encoding.
  Characters such as &, #, +, % or message-id characters truncate or
  corrupt the query, and a filter like a&per_page=100 injects parameters.
  Use the reqwest query builder.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_submit), the help text says
  the default is HEAD if in a git repo, but no repo check or local
  resolution is done. The server resolves HEAD in its own repository from
  settings.git.repository_path, so the user may get a review of the wrong
  commit or an opaque failure with no warning.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_submit), mbox input is read
  with read_to_string for both files and stdin. Any non-UTF-8 byte, such as
  legacy 8-bit mailing-list encodings, fails with an error that does not
  mention encoding. With no INPUT and non-terminal stdin (cron, CI) the CLI
  also silently switches to stdin mode and may block or submit empty
  content. Read bytes and convert lossily.

- [MEDIUM] The new src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs has no tests. Submit-type
  detection, stdin default, subject truncation, page arithmetic and
  format_timestamp are inlined in async handlers and cannot be unit tested.
  The Serialize and Deserialize derives on SubmitRequest in src/api.rs also
  leave the CLI and server wire format unpinned. Add serde round-trip tests
  for Inject, Remote and RemoteRange.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (main), the NOT_FOUND and BAD_REQUEST
  hints are dead code, because handlers turn non-success responses into
  anyhow strings and never call error_for_status. Errors and hints are also
  printed to stdout, so with --format json scripts receive non-JSON text on
  stdout instead of stderr.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_submit), s.contains(..) is tested
  before the file existence check, so a path like ../series.mbox is
  submitted as a Range. With --type given and no input, the target becomes
  HEAD for every type, so --type mbox reads a file named HEAD instead of
  stdin.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (print_colored), set_color, write! and
  reset are unwrapped. A closed stdout pipe, for example list piped to
  head, panics, and in the main error path this masks the original error.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_show), a failed /api/review
  fetch has no else branch, so a 404 or 500 yields no review summary and no
  warning, indistinguishable from a patchset without a review. A missing
  status also becomes an empty string that skips the review fetch.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_list and handle_show), untrusted
  subjects, authors, apply_error, summaries, logs and failed_reason are
  printed raw in text mode. ANSI or OSC escape sequences can spoof the
  status column, hide rows or write to the clipboard of the operator
  terminal. Strip control characters before printing. JSON mode is safe.

- [LOW] Commit message d67c8bd2 quotes sashiko-cli, file paths, chrono,
  clap and Deserialize in backticks, which repository commit standards
  forbid and cargo fmt and clippy do not check.

findings.problem: list panics slicing subject at non-char-boundary byte 45
findings.explanation: handle_list in src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs guards with subject.len() > 48 (bytes) and then slices &subject[..45]. If byte 45 falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character, str slicing panics. Patchset subjects come from untrusted mailing-list mail and are often non-ASCII, so one such patchset on the requested page aborts sashiko-cli list mid-table and the rest of the page is lost. The impact is limited to the CLI, not the daemon, so Medium. The {:<50} padding is also byte-width based and misaligns non-ASCII text. Truncate with chars().take() or floor_char_boundary.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Byte-indexed slice of untrusted text without a char-boundary check panics on multi-byte characters.

findings.problem: settings fallback retries same call then panics
findings.explanation: main() runs Settings::new().unwrap_or_else(|_| Settings::new().expect(...)). The fallback re-invokes the identical call, so it fails exactly when it is needed and expect() panics. Settings::new() reads a required Settings.toml from the CWD and deserializes the full daemon Settings. Running the CLI outside the server directory, or with a malformed file, panics with a backtrace even when --server or SASHIKO_SERVER is given and settings are only needed for the default URL and repo path. The code comment promises a fallback to defaults that does not exist, and no test covers it. The settings guide expects a missing file to fall back to http://127.0.0.1:8080 and a malformed file to fail loudly with a clear error; this does neither.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The documented fallback is a no-op retry that panics.

findings.problem: list filter and show id spliced into URLs without encoding
findings.explanation: handle_list appends the filter with url.push_str(&format!('&q={}', q)), and handle_show builds /api/patch?id={} and /api/review?id={} from the raw id. Values containing &, #, +, %, spaces or message-id characters (<, >, @, +) truncate, split or corrupt the query. A filter like a&per_page=100 injects parameters, and a message-id passed to show is looked up wrongly. The result is a silently wrong or empty listing or a confusing URL error. Input comes from the invoking user, so exploitability is low. Use reqwest .query(&[...]).

User-supplied id, possibly a message-id, is not encoded.

findings.problem: HTTP status hints are dead code and errors go to stdout
findings.explanation: Every handler turns a non-success response into an anyhow error string and never calls error_for_status(). The downcast to reqwest::Error followed by req_err.status() branch in main() for NOT_FOUND and BAD_REQUEST therefore never fires; only the is_connect() hint is reachable. Errors and hints are printed to stdout, so with --format json a script gets non-JSON text on stdout instead of stderr. The result is poor error reporting and polluted machine-readable output, with no data impact.

findings.explanation: The help text says Defaults to HEAD if in a git repo, but handle_submit never checks for a git repo or resolves HEAD locally. With no input and a terminal stdin it sends Remote with sha HEAD and repo settings.git.repository_path to the server, which resolves HEAD in its own repository rather than the user checkout. The user gets a review of the wrong commit, or an opaque failure if the path is absent on the server, with no warning. The semantic is undocumented in the commit message.

findings.problem: mbox submit uses read_to_string and rejects non-UTF-8 input
findings.explanation: Both std::fs::read_to_string and Stdin::read_to_string return InvalidData on any non-UTF-8 byte. Real mailing-list mbox files often contain Latin-1 or other legacy 8-bit encodings, so such patches cannot be submitted, and the error message does not mention encoding. Also, with no INPUT and non-terminal stdin (cron, CI, wrappers) the CLI selects stdin mbox mode and blocks or submits empty content, so the HEAD default only holds interactively. Reading bytes and converting lossily would be more robust.

findings.problem: show passes patchset id to /api/review, which expects a review id
findings.explanation: Medium: this is a contained functional bug in the new CLI that makes 'sashiko-cli show' display the wrong review, or none. It does not corrupt data or cross a security boundary. Verified in code: api.rs get_review (line 355) parses the id as i64 and logs 'Fetching details for review id', then calls state.db.get_review_details(id_val). In db.rs, get_review_details (line 2342) runs 'FROM reviews r ... WHERE r.id = ?', so the key is reviews.id. The same query also selects r.patch_id, which shows reviews is a separate table with its own id sequence and a foreign key to the patch. handle_show in sashiko-cli.rs (line 416) builds '{}/api/review?id={}' from the id used for /api/patch (the patchset id, or latest.id from /api/patchsets). The ids come from different tables, so they only coincide by accident. When they differ, the CLI either gets 404 (no review is shown) or gets another patchset's review. In the second case it prints that review's verdict, model and summary under this patchset's header. This is the common case once any patchset has been re-reviewed or has several reviews, or when some patchsets have no review row. It affects the 'Reviewed', 'Failed' and 'Failed To Apply' states. The bug is introduced by this patch, so it is not preexisting. The wrong-id premise is confirmed, not discarded: get_review_details keys by review id, not patchset id. A correct fix is to read the review id from the 'reviews' array in the /api/patch response and query /api/review with that id.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Sends the patchset id (from the user argument or from /api/patchsets items[0].id) to an endpoint that interprets it as a review id.
The endpoint treats the id as a review id and has no patchset fallback.
The lookup is keyed by reviews.id, not patchset id, so a patchset id returns an unrelated review or nothing.

findings.problem: submit defaults to literal HEAD, so every submission collides on one id
findings.explanation: Medium: this is a contained functional defect that misattributes or silently drops repeat submissions. It does not corrupt unrelated data or cross a security boundary. The mechanism, read in the code: (1) In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs, handle_submit falls back to (SubmitType::Remote, "HEAD") when no input is given and stdin is a terminal, and sends that symbolic string in SubmitRequest::Remote { sha: "HEAD", repo }. (2) In src/api.rs, submit_patch does `let id = sha.clone();` and calls create_fetching_patchset(&id, ...) with no rev-parse resolution. (3) In src/db.rs, create_fetching_patchset builds root_msg_id = "HEAD@sashiko.local" and looks up an existing patchset by cover_letter_message_id. If one exists, it returns the old id. It resets to Fetching only when the status is Failed or Fetching. If the earlier HEAD patchset is Pending, Incomplete or Reviewed, nothing is created or updated, yet the API still answers status=accepted with id=HEAD. (4) src/fetcher.rs never resolves the ref. It runs `git fetch <remote> HEAD`, then extract_patch("HEAD", "HEAD", 1, 1) with the literal string as article_id and message_id. src/main.rs groups these by article_id into the same root_msg_id. The consequence is that a user running the CLI at two different times, after the server repo HEAD or the remote HEAD has moved, gets the second submission attached to the first HEAD patchset, or ignored. The id also shows the wrong commit, and which commit gets reviewed depends on when the fetcher ticks (every 10s), not on when the user submitted. In the same state, concurrent HEAD submissions are deduplicated by the fetcher's HashSet. I did not read the PatchSubmitted ingestion path in main.rs to confirm how the second event with message_id "HEAD" is deduplicated or overwritten, so that part is unverified. This is why I cap it at Medium. The CLI default is new in this commit, so the finding is not preexisting. The server-side lack of resolution already existed, but the CLI now makes symbolic refs the default input.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The CLI sends an unresolved symbolic ref as the sha, and does so by default when no input is given.
The user-supplied string is used verbatim as the patchset identity and the response id, with no rev-parse resolution.
A second HEAD submission finds the existing row and returns it unchanged unless it is Failed or Fetching, so a later submission of a different commit is not tracked separately.
The fetcher uses the literal ref as the article_id and message_id and never resolves it to a SHA, so identity depends on what HEAD points to when the fetcher runs.

findings.problem: handle_list slices subject at byte 45, panics on multibyte UTF-8
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the CLI crashes with a panic, which hurts UX, but only the `list` subcommand is affected and the daemon is untouched, so this is a contained functional bug and not High. The candidate's arithmetic premise is wrong (see the dismissal), but the same function, handle_list, has a real panic. It does `if subject.len() > 48 { format!("{}...", &subject[..45]) }`. `len()` counts bytes and the slice is by byte offset. If byte 45 falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character, the slice panics. Subjects come from patch emails and PR titles, which are untrusted and regularly contain non-ASCII text (accented names, CJK, emoji). A single such patchset on the requested page makes `sashiko-cli list` panic instead of printing the table. This violates patterns/error-handling.md section 1 (UTF-8 string slicing). The code is new in this patch, so it is not preexisting. I did not run the CLI; the conclusion follows from reading the slice expression, and `PatchsetRow.subject` is filled from ingested message subjects.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Byte-offset slice of an untrusted, possibly non-ASCII subject without a char-boundary check panics the CLI.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: Remote and RemoteRange share one server arm in submit_patch, so a range such as a..b may be fetched as a single invalid revision and range submission fails end to end; --baseline is silently ignored for non-mbox submissions.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: 1) The shared arm is intentional. submit_patch in src/api.rs forwards sha unchanged as FetchRequest.commit_hash for both variants, and the range handling lives in FetchAgent::process_queue in src/fetcher.rs. That function branches on commit_or_range.contains(".."). For a range it runs git rev-list --count (rejecting 0 or more than 100 commits) and git rev-list --reverse, then calls extract_patch for each SHA with index and total set. A single commit goes through the else branch. Ranges are therefore handled correctly after the shared arm, and the CLI Range type (sha: target) reaches that branch. 2) The optimistic fetch_commits passes a..b to git fetch as an argument, which is likely to fail. process_queue then falls back to fetch_all, so the range is still fetched. That is only a performance inefficiency and was not the claimed failure. The range is not treated as a single invalid revision. 3) --baseline is documented as 'Baseline commit (for mbox injection only)' in the Submit clap args. Remote and range submissions derive base_commit from the commit parent in extract_patch (rev-parse commit^). Ignoring --baseline for those types is documented behavior, not a silent contract break. 4) This is a single commit, not a series, so no later patch needs to be checked. The candidate's range-failure claim is disproved by the fetcher code; the baseline claim is documented behavior.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: sashiko-cli submit posts to /api/submit with no credential (no local token, no bearer JWT), so a default server may answer 403 under the Permission::Ingest model in the api-auth guide.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: The candidate assumes submit_patch gates on is_authorized with Permission::Ingest. At this commit it does not. I read src/api.rs lines 150-280 at d67c8bd2: submit_patch checks state.read_only, then rejects any peer whose address is not loopback, and nothing else. A grep of src/ for is_authorized, presents_local_token and local_token found no definitions or uses, and src/auth.rs and src/access.rs do not exist (git_ls of src/ lists neither). The credential model the candidate cites is therefore not part of this tree, so the CLI cannot be missing a credential that the server never checks. The CLI builds its URL from settings.server.host and settings.server.port, or from --server / SASHIKO_SERVER, so a default local invocation connects from a loopback peer and passes the check. A git_log of d67c8bd2..HEAD returned no later commits, so no later patch changes this contract. A non-loopback --server would get a 403 from the server's own loopback-only policy, which is pre-existing server behaviour this commit does not touch. The remaining complaint, that the CLI prints an opaque 'Submission failed (403): ...', is a minor message-quality issue and is not the authorization defect the candidate claims.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: handle_list computes (data.total + data.per_page - 1) / data.per_page with a server-echoed per_page, so --per-page 0 would cause underflow or divide-by-zero, and the sum could overflow.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: A grep for PatchsetsResponse at the target revision shows one construction site, `Ok(Json(PatchsetsResponse {` in list_patchsets at src/api.rs:290. The other matches are the struct definition and the two CLI deserialization sites. In list_patchsets, per_page is computed as `pagination.per_page.unwrap_or(50).clamp(1, 100)` (src/api.rs:271) and that same variable is placed in the response (src/api.rs:294). So a Sashiko server always echoes per_page in 1..=100. `--per-page 0` from the CLI is therefore clamped to 1 server-side. With per_page >= 1, `per_page - 1` cannot underflow, the divisor is nonzero, and the addition cannot realistically overflow because total is a row count. The remaining scenario needs a non-Sashiko or hostile server supplied by the user through --server or SASHIKO_SERVER. That is an endpoint the user chose, and it crosses no Sashiko security boundary, so it is not a defect in the patch. The `/api/patch` and `/api/review` paths are not involved in this arithmetic.

B.summary:
This change adds sashiko-cli, a new command-line client for the Sashiko
server, so users can submit patches, check server status, and browse
patchsets without hand-writing HTTP requests. To let the client parse
server replies and build request bodies, it also derives Deserialize (and
Serialize on SubmitRequest) for the API and database structs in
src/api.rs and src/db.rs, and adds chrono plus clap's env feature to
Cargo.toml.

The client has four subcommands: submit, status, list, and show. Submit
auto-detects its input type: "-" or a piped stdin means an mbox, anything
containing ".." is a commit range, an existing file is an mbox, and
anything else is treated as a single remote commit. The server URL comes
from --server, the SASHIKO_SERVER environment variable, or the host and
port in the settings. Output is colored text by default, or pretty JSON
with --format json.

Before:
  There was no CLI. Submitting a patch or reading status meant sending
  requests to the server's HTTP endpoints by hand, for example:
    curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/submit -d '{"type":"remote",...}'

After:
  $ sashiko-cli submit HEAD~3..HEAD
  Success: Submission accepted. ID: <id>

  $ sashiko-cli status
  Server Status:
    Version:   ...
    Messages:  ...
    Patchsets: ...
  Queue Breakdown:
    Pending         ...

  $ sashiko-cli list pending --per-page 10
  prints a table of ID, Status, Subject and Date, then "Page N of M".

  $ sashiko-cli show latest
  prints patchset details, per-patch status and any review summary.

  On failure, the error message is printed to stdout (not stderr), with
  a hint for connection failures, and the process exits with code 1.
B.inline_review:
- [HIGH] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_show), the patchset id (or a
  message-id) is sent to /api/review, but src/api.rs get_review parses a
  numeric review id and src/db.rs get_review_details filters on reviews.id,
  not the patchset id. show and show latest therefore display (or merge into
  the JSON output) a review belonging to a different patchset, with no error.
  For a message-id the server returns 400, which the CLI drops. The correct
  review ids are already in the reviews array of the /api/patch response,
  which the CLI never reads.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (main), the Settings::new() fallback in
  unwrap_or_else repeats the identical failing call and panics via expect.
  When Settings.toml is missing or not in the cwd (cron, systemd, installed
  exe), the CLI dies with exit 101 and the original ConfigError is lost. The
  load happens before --server or SASHIKO_SERVER is read, so they cannot
  rescue status, list or show. The comment claims a fallback to defaults.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_list), the subject is truncated
  with a byte slice at offset 45 after a byte-length test. A non-ASCII
  subject with a multi-byte character straddling byte 45 panics and aborts
  the table. Subjects come from mailing-list mail, so this is routine input
  and can be crafted deliberately. Truncate on chars instead.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (main, print_colored), the Error line
  and hint lines are written to stdout, even with --format json. A script
  piping sashiko-cli --format json list to a JSON parser gets non-JSON text
  in its data stream. Every failure also exits 1, so callers cannot tell a
  refused connection from a 403 or 404. Diagnostics belong on stderr.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_list, handle_show), the list
  filter and the show id are interpolated raw into URLs. A filter containing
  &, #, + or % is truncated or split into extra parameters, and message-ids
  with <, > or + are mangled, so the server filters on something other than
  what was typed and the user sees a plausible empty list or a 404. Use the
  reqwest query builder.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_show), a non-success response
  from /api/review is silently dropped: there is no else branch. The text
  output omits the Review Summary and the JSON output lacks the review key,
  with no warning and exit 0, so a server error looks the same as no stored
  review.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_submit), auto-detection tests
  for '..' before checking that the path exists. An existing mbox such as
  ../patches/0001.mbox or my..series.mbox is sent as a RemoteRange with the
  path as the sha, and the file is never read. Also, --type mbox with no
  input falls back to the target HEAD and reads a file named HEAD, and
  --baseline is silently ignored for remote and range submissions.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (main), the reqwest Client is built with
  Client::new(), which has no connect or total timeout. A server that accepts
  the connection but never answers makes every subcommand hang forever, so
  cron jobs and scripts stall with no error. Set connect_timeout and timeout.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_show), the Verdict block reads a
  verdict key from the /api/review body, but src/db.rs get_review_details
  builds a fixed JSON object (result, status, inline_review, summary, logs,
  and so on) with no verdict, and src/api.rs get_review passes it through
  unchanged. The Verdict line and its LGTM/Request Changes colouring never
  print, so a review that requested changes looks the same as one that
  passed. The CLI ignores the status and result keys that carry the outcome.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_submit) with src/api.rs
  (submit_patch), submit with no input in a terminal, --type remote with no
  input, or a range prints Success with ID HEAD or the range string. The
  server keys the placeholder as <id>@sashiko.local, but show looks up the
  bare id, so the returned ID cannot be used to track the submission. HEAD is
  sent unresolved and evaluated by src/fetcher.rs in the server's repository,
  not the user's checkout, despite the help text. The raw string also acts as
  the dedupe key, so a later HEAD submission reuses the old row and can
  overwrite the earlier patch diff.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_status) with src/api.rs
  (get_stats), status presents zeros as authoritative. The CLI defaults
  missing breakdown keys to 0, never checks the status field, and omits the
  cancelled bucket the server emits, so the buckets do not sum to Patchsets.
  Separately, get_stats converts DB errors into zero counts with HTTP 200 and
  status ok; that server-side swallowing was not introduced by this change
  (pre-existing), but this CLI is the first consumer to display it as fact.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_list, handle_show,
  handle_submit), server-sourced text (subjects, authors, apply errors,
  review summaries, logs, and error bodies) is printed raw in text mode,
  which is the default. Escape sequences in a mail-derived subject or author
  can rewrite the terminal, forge coloured lines or emit OSC sequences when a
  maintainer runs list, show or submit. Nothing in src strips control
  characters. Replace control characters before printing.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_submit), the mbox is read with
  read_to_string into a String-typed Inject.raw. A UTF-8 BOM before the first
  'From ' line (common from PowerShell output) prevents the ingestor
  is_mbox_separator from recognising the first separator, so the first
  message may be misparsed or dropped after a Success message. Non-UTF-8
  bytes (for example a Latin-1 diff) are refused at the CLI although the
  server ingest path is byte-oriented. Strip a leading BOM and report the
  encoding on failure.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_submit), the repo value is sent
  unresolved from --repo or settings.git.repository_path, and the server
  uses it as a git remote URL inside its own repo (src/fetcher.rs
  ensure_remote). The default Settings.toml value third_party/linux is
  relative, so it resolves to a nonexistent nested path, and tilde, relative
  or Windows paths are not meaningful to the server. The CLI has already
  printed Submission accepted, and the failure only appears later in server
  logs or patchset status.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_list), the subject is sliced at
  byte 45 after a byte-length check, so a multi-byte character straddling
  that offset panics and hides the whole page. The default list command hits
  this path whenever one row has such a subject. Overlaps the earlier
  handle_list panic finding; truncate on chars and count chars.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (main, handle_list, handle_show,
  handle_status), the NOT_FOUND and BAD_REQUEST hints are dead code. The
  handlers return plain anyhow string errors, so the downcast to
  reqwest::Error never sees a status (nothing calls error_for_status). The
  status, list and show handlers also discard the response body, so users
  see only a bare status code.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (print_colored), set_color, write! and
  reset are unwrapped, and the handlers use println!, so a closed pipe such
  as sashiko-cli list | head ends in a panic message instead of a quiet
  exit.

- [LOW] The commit adds the 526-line src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs and Deserialize
  derives on server types in src/api.rs and src/db.rs with no tests or
  fixtures. Input auto-detection (handle_submit), URL building, truncation,
  pagination arithmetic, and the SubmitRequest wire tags are unpinned, so
  the panic, the '..' ordering and the unencoded query would not fail any
  test.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (main), the base URL is built from
  settings.server.host, but src/api.rs run_server always binds 0.0.0.0 and
  ignores host. A wildcard host fails to connect on Windows, and a LAN IP
  reaches the server as a non-loopback peer, so submit_patch returns an
  empty 403 and the CLI shows no cause. A trailing slash on --server
  probably yields // paths, which was not verified. Map wildcard hosts to
  127.0.0.1, trim the slash, and explain 403.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_submit), submit with no INPUT reads
  stdin whenever it is not a terminal, which overrides the documented HEAD
  default in cron, systemd, CI and scheduled tasks. With stdin on /dev/null
  the CLI posts an empty mbox and the server returns a bare 400 that does
  not mention stdin. With an open stdin that never closes it hangs
  indefinitely. Require an explicit '-' and refuse empty content.

findings.problem: settings fallback repeats the failing call and panics
findings.explanation: Any run where Settings.toml is missing, incomplete or not in the cwd (cron, systemd, an installed .exe on Windows, a kernel checkout) panics with exit 101 and a generic message, and the original ConfigError is discarded. The load happens before cli.server is read, so --server and SASHIKO_SERVER cannot rescue status, list or show. The comment says it falls back to defaults, but the closure calls the same Settings::new(), which cannot succeed where the first call failed.

findings.problem: list slices subject at byte 45 and panics on UTF-8
findings.explanation: sashiko-cli list aborts mid-table with a panic whenever a subject longer than 48 bytes has a multi-byte character straddling byte 45. Subjects come from mailing-list mail and injected mbox files, so non-ASCII text is routine, and a sender can craft one deliberately. The guard subject.len() > 48 counts bytes and the slice uses a byte offset with no char-boundary check. Fix with char_indices or chars().take(45).

locations.why_this_location_matters: Byte-index slice of server-supplied, possibly non-ASCII text.

findings.problem: errors and hints go to stdout, even with --format json
findings.explanation: On any failure main() writes 'Error: ...' and the hint lines to stdout through print_colored (StandardStream::stdout) and println!, then exits 1. A script running sashiko-cli --format json list | jq gets non-JSON text in the stream it parses and a parser error that hides the real failure. Every failure uses exit code 1, so callers cannot tell a refused connection from a 403 or 404 without scraping text. Diagnostics belong on stderr.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Failure text goes to the result stream, including under --format json.
The helper can only write to stdout and is used for errors as well as results.

findings.problem: 404/400 hints are dead code and error bodies are dropped
findings.explanation: Every handler turns a non-success status into an anyhow string error. main() then downcasts to reqwest::Error and checks status(), which is Some only for errors built by error_for_status(), and nothing here calls it. The status, list and show handlers also drop the response body, so the user sees a bare status code.

findings.problem: list filter and show id are put in URLs unencoded
findings.explanation: list FILTER is appended as &q={} and show ID goes into ?id={} (and the review URL) raw. A filter containing &, #, +, % or a space is truncated, split into extra parameters (a&per_page=100) or reinterpreted, so the server filters on something other than what was typed and the user sees a plausible No items found or a 404. Message-ids, which the server accepts as ids, contain <, >, @ and +. Use reqwest .query().

findings.problem: show silently drops a failed review fetch and exits 0
findings.explanation: For Reviewed, Failed and Failed To Apply patchsets handle_show requests /api/review and keeps the result only on success. findings.problem: show passes patchset id to /api/review, which keys on reviews.id
findings.explanation: Consequence: `sashiko-cli show <id>` (and `show latest`) displays, or in JSON mode merges into `details.review`, the review whose reviews.id equals the patchset id. That review can belong to a different patchset, so the CLI reports a false verdict, summary and logs with no error. It is reachable on every `show` of a patchset whose status is Reviewed, Failed or Failed To Apply, which is the primary use of the command. Proof: `src/api.rs` get_review parses `query.id` as i64 and calls `state.db.get_review_details(id_val)`, otherwise it returns BAD_REQUEST. `src/db.rs` get_review_details runs `FROM reviews r ... WHERE r.id = ?`, so the key is the review row id. `handle_show` in `src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs` builds `format!("{}/api/review?id={}", base_url, id)` with `id` being the patchset id, either user-supplied or taken from `/api/patchsets` items for `latest`. The id spaces diverge: reviews has its own INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, and `reviews.patchset_id` links it to a patchset. A patchset can have zero, one or many reviews, because the review pipeline creates one per patch or retry. The right id is already in the `/api/patch` response: `get_patchset_details` returns a `reviews` array whose entries carry `id` (selected as `r.id`), ordered by created_at ASC, and the CLI never reads it. Secondary effects on the same path: (1) when `id` is a message-id, `/api/patch` resolves it via get_patchset_details_by_msgid, but `/api/review` returns 400 for the non-numeric id; the CLI only checks `is_success()` and silently drops the review, so the Review Summary is missing with no warning. (2) A 404 for a nonexistent review id is also swallowed silently. (3) The Logs section is gated on the patchset status, but the logs come from the wrong review. The preconditions are normal ones: any deployment with more than one patchset, where ids rarely coincide. Not preexisting, because `sashiko-cli.rs` is new in this commit. The commit message claims the tool supports 'viewing patchset details' and the diff includes no test or evidence of an end-to-end check. Fix: take the review id from `details["reviews"]` (for example the latest entry, or the one matching a patch) and call `/api/review` with that, or print the `reviews` array directly. Treat a non-success response as an error or warn on stderr rather than dropping it.

findings.problem: show reads a verdict key that /api/review never emits
findings.explanation: Consequence: `sashiko-cli show <id>` for a reviewed patchset never prints the Verdict line or its LGTM (green) / Request Changes (red) colouring, and the text output gives no indication that the review outcome was dropped. The reader sees a Review Summary with only Model and the summary text, so a review that requested changes looks the same as one that passed. Reachability: every `sashiko-cli show` (including the default `latest`) on a patchset whose status is Reviewed, Failed or Failed To Apply, in text format. Proof: `handle_show` fetches `/api/review?id=...` and does `review.get("verdict").and_then(|v| v.as_str())`. The route `/api/review` is `get_review`, which returns `Json(details)` from `Database::get_review_details` unchanged. That function builds the JSON from a fixed `serde_json::json!` object with keys id, model, summary, created_at, input, output, baseline, provider, prompts_hash, result, status, inline_review, logs, tokens_in, tokens_out, patch_id and tokens_cached. There is no verdict key. A tree-wide grep for `verdict` at this commit matches only src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (lines 472, 473, 479), so no other producer exists. The `if let Some` therefore always falls through silently. The keys that carry the review outcome are `status` and `result` (from reviews.result_description), plus `inline_review`, and the CLI ignores all of them. The `match verdict` arms ("LGTM", "Request Changes") also encode strings no producer in this tree emits. This is a one-sided contract: the consumer was written against a shape the server does not produce. The commit message presents the CLI as supporting patchset details and gives no evidence it was run against a server with a reviewed patchset. Severity is Medium: a contained functional defect in a read-only CLI display that silently omits information, with no money, credential or store impact. It is not higher because the Failed and Failed To Apply states are still shown through the patchset status and failure reason. If the verdict is meant to be derived (for example from `result` or `status`), the CLI should read that key; otherwise the server should emit it.

Producer of the /api/review body; its fixed key set (result, status, inline_review, ...) contains no verdict.

findings.problem: submit HEAD/range id untrackable, resolves server HEAD
findings.explanation:
Consequence and reach: `sashiko-cli submit` with no input in a terminal, or `--type remote` with no input, or a range such as `a..b`, prints 'Success: Submission accepted. ID: HEAD' (or the range string). That ID cannot be used to track the submission, and for HEAD it names a different commit than the user expects. Nothing in the code cannot be shown to reach this: `handle_submit` is the only CLI submit path, and the server route is the only consumer.

1) The returned ID does not locate the placeholder. `submit_patch` sets `let id = sha.clone()` and returns it as `SubmitResponse.id`. `create_fetching_patchset` stores the placeholder under `cover_letter_message_id = '<id>@sashiko.local'`. `sashiko-cli show <id>` calls `/api/patch?id=HEAD`. `get_patchset` finds that `HEAD` does not parse as i64 and calls `get_patchset_details_by_msgid('HEAD')`. That queries `cover_letter_message_id = 'HEAD'` (no suffix), then `patches.message_id = 'HEAD'`. Both miss, so the result is 404. The same happens for range strings. A 40-hex single SHA only becomes findable after ingestion, via the patches.message_id fallback, because the fetcher sets `message_id = sha`. A failure is recorded under `HEAD@sashiko.local` by `update_patchset_error`, but the user cannot reach it with the ID they were given. The CLI has already printed Success before any fetch happens.

2) HEAD is not the user's HEAD. The help text says it 'Defaults to HEAD if in a git repo', but the CLI never inspects the cwd or resolves the ref. It sends the literal `HEAD` with `repo = settings.git.repository_path` (or `--repo`). In `FetchAgent::extract_patch` the commit is passed to `git show HEAD` and `git rev-parse HEAD^` with `current_dir(self.repo_path)`, which is the server's configured repository. The review therefore targets the server repo's local HEAD, not the commit the user meant. `git fetch <remote> HEAD` only populates FETCH_HEAD and is never consulted.

3) Identity collision. The raw string `HEAD` is the dedupe key at three levels. The placeholder is `HEAD@sashiko.local`. The `FetchAgent` queue is a `HashSet<String>` of commit strings. The patch row uses `message_id = 'HEAD'`, and `create_patch` does `ON CONFLICT(message_id) DO UPDATE SET patchset_id, part_index, diff`. A second `submit` of HEAD after the repo has moved reuses the existing patchset; `create_fetching_patchset` only resets status when it is Failed or Fetching, otherwise it returns the old row id. The new diff then overwrites the previous HEAD patch row, so an earlier Reviewed patchset can silently end up showing a different commit's diff. I did not trace every later ingestion step in `process_parsed_article`, so the exact end state of the status field is unverified; the overwrite via ON CONFLICT is confirmed in the code read.

The server-side `id = sha.clone()` behaviour predates this commit, but the CLI is what makes symbolic refs and ranges the default and advertised path, so the defect is introduced by this change. Medium: it misleads the user about what was submitted and how to follow it, but needs no money, credential or store-corruption path beyond the review DB, and the submit route is loopback-only. Fix direction: resolve the ref (`git rev-parse`) in the CLI against the user's repo, or in the server before keying, and return the numeric patchset id from `create_fetching_patchset` in `SubmitResponse`.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Sends an unresolved symbolic ref with the server-settings repo path; no git-repo check despite the help text.
The raw client string becomes both the placeholder key and the ID returned to the user.
The stored key carries a suffix that get_patchset_details_by_msgid does not add, so the returned ID misses the placeholder; repeats reuse the same row.
Runs in the server's repo_path, so HEAD resolves to the server repo's HEAD, not the user's checkout.

findings.problem: status shows zeros from a failing DB and omits cancelled
findings.explanation: Consequence and reachability: `sashiko-cli status` (new in this commit) calls GET /api/stats and prints the result as the server's authoritative state. `get_stats` in src/api.rs converts any DB error into zero counts with HTTP 200 and `"status": "ok"`. `count_messages(None, None).await.unwrap_or(0)` and `count_patchsets(None, None).await.unwrap_or(0)` turn a failed query into 0. `get_patchset_counts_by_status().await.unwrap_or_default()` turns a failure into an empty map, so every breakdown bucket becomes 0 through `counts.get(..).unwrap_or(&0)`. The handler has no error path, since its return type is `Json<serde_json::Value>`. A caller therefore cannot tell a locked, corrupt or unreachable database from an empty healthy server. The CLI adds a second layer: `breakdown.get(key).unwrap_or(&zero)` hides any missing key as 0, and `handle_status` never inspects the `status` field. An operator or script running `sashiko-cli status` during a DB outage sees 'Messages: 0, Patchsets: 0' and all-zero queue counts, which reads as an idle, healthy system. The `--format json` output passes the same zeros through for scripts. Second defect: `get_stats` emits `breakdown.cancelled` (`let cancelled = *counts.get("Cancelled")...` and `"cancelled": cancelled`), but the CLI's `items` array stops at `incomplete`. Cancelled patchsets are counted in `Patchsets` but never shown, so the displayed buckets do not sum to the total. Preexisting split: the server-side swallowing predates this commit, because the diff only adds Deserialize derives to api.rs and does not touch `get_stats`. The CLI's silent default and the missing `cancelled` row are introduced here, and the CLI is the first consumer to present the zeros as authoritative. findings.problem: base URL built from server.host, which the server ignores
findings.explanation: Consequence: with a wildcard or non-loopback server.host, the CLI cannot reach the server, or submit is refused, and the printed hint blames the wrong cause. Reachability: this needs an operator to edit host, because the checked-in Settings.toml sets host = "127.0.0.1" and no deploy config in .github or README sets it, so the default setup is unaffected. It is a contained usability defect with no data or money risk, hence Low. Verified: (1) run_server in src/api.rs:142 binds SocketAddr::from(([0, 0, 0, 0], settings.port)) and never reads settings.host, so host is a dead setting for the server, and a user may set 0.0.0.0 to match what the server really does. SASHIKO_SERVER__HOST also overrides it through the config crate. (2) main in src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs:115-117 formats http://{host}:{port} straight from that value when --server and SASHIKO_SERVER are absent. Connecting to 0.0.0.0 fails on Windows with WSAEADDRNOTAVAIL, while Linux routes it to localhost. That Windows behaviour is platform knowledge, not something this repo can demonstrate. The CLI then prints the hint 'Is the Sashiko server running'. A specific non-loopback host such as a LAN IP reaches the server, but the connection's peer address is then that LAN IP. submit_patch (src/api.rs:176-181) requires addr.ip().is_loopback() and returns a bare StatusCode::FORBIDDEN with no body. handle_submit then reports 'Submission failed (403 Forbidden): ' with an empty body. The CLI's status-based hints in main are dead code for this case, because the error is an anyhow! string, not a reqwest error with a status, so no explanation is shown. Not confirmed: a trailing slash on --server yields //api/... paths; the routes are registered exactly and no path normalisation layer appears in run_server, so this is likely a 404, but I did not verify axum's behaviour with a test. The --server help text says the default is 127.0.0.1:8080, but the code uses the settings value; this is accurate only for the checked-in config. A fix would map 0.0.0.0 or :: to 127.0.0.1 when building the URL, trim trailing slashes from --server, and have the 403 path return an explanatory body or have the CLI print a hint on 403.

locations.why_this_location_matters: A listen address from settings is reused as a connect address without normalising wildcards, and --server is used without trimming a trailing slash.
The server always binds all interfaces and ignores settings.host, so the host value cannot be relied on as a connect address.
Refuses with an empty 403 body, so the CLI shows no reason when the URL host is not loopback.

findings.problem: server-sourced text printed to terminal without sanitizing
findings.explanation: Consequence: a patch author who can get a mail into the ingested lists can put ESC/CSI/OSC bytes in a subject or author header, or steer model output into a review summary or log, and have the maintainer's terminal interpret them when they run `sashiko-cli list`, `show` or `submit`. That can rewrite or hide earlier lines, forge the coloured Verdict line, or emit title and clipboard OSC sequences. Reachability: `handle_list` prints `subject_display` for every row, and `handle_show` prints `details["subject"]`, `details["author"]`, per-patch `subject` and `apply_error`, `failed_reason`, the review `summary`, `model` and `logs`. `handle_submit` echoes the raw server error body through `anyhow!("Submission failed ({}): {}", status, text)`, which `main` prints with `println!`. Verification: `git_grep` over `src/` at d67c8bd for `is_control|sanitize|strip_ansi|escape_default|escape_debug` returned no matches, so neither the ingestion/API code nor the CLI strips control characters, and the repo has no sanitizer the CLI could call. The values are deserialized as plain `String` or `serde_json::Value` and printed with `println!`/`print!`. The text format is the default (`default_value = "text"`), so the default output path is the exposed one. `--format json` goes through `serde_json::to_string_pretty`, which escapes control characters, so it is not affected. Mitigations and limits: this is a human-facing CLI, not parsed by other programs, and exploitation needs a maintainer to view attacker-influenced data, so I rate it Medium, not High. It is not preexisting because the CLI is new in this commit. A fix would be a small helper that replaces `char::is_control` characters (other than newline/tab where wanted) with a visible placeholder, applied to every server-sourced string before printing. Note on a related defect in the same lines: `&subject[..45]` in `handle_list` slices by byte offset and panics on a multi-byte character straddling byte 45, so a non-ASCII subject crashes `list`.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Mail-derived subject written raw to the terminal; the author line at 435 and the patch subject at 454 do the same.
Every listed subject is printed unsanitized, so one crafted patch affects each `list` run.
The raw server error body is echoed to the terminal by main's println!.

findings.problem: mbox read as UTF-8 only; BOM defeats split_mbox, non-UTF-8 refused
findings.explanation: Consequence: on Windows, mbox files produced by PowerShell can be rejected or mis-split, so a patch is not submitted or is parsed wrongly. Reachability: `sashiko-cli submit <file>` or stdin, the documented path for `git format-patch` output. It is operator-triggered, not a loop, so Medium. The candidate is partly wrong. (1) CRLF is tolerated. `split_mbox` splits on b'\n' bytes, `is_mbox_separator` only counts colons, `extract_message_id` uses `lines()`, and the `patch.rs` tests parse `\r\n` messages. (2) A UTF-16LE file, which PowerShell 5.1 `>` produces, fails loudly: `read_to_string` errors, `main` prints `Error: ...` and exits 1. That is not a silent failure. The real defects are: (a) A UTF-8 BOM, from `Out-File -Encoding utf8` or a BOM-bearing file, survives `read_to_string`. `is_mbox_separator` requires `line.starts_with(b"From ")`, so the first line `\u{feff}From <sha> ...` is not recognised as a separator. It is appended to the first message as body or header text, and `Inject` is posted with it intact. The server guardrail `raw.contains("From ")` still passes, so the server accepts it with 200 and an ID. Whether `parse_email` (mail-parser) then recovers the first message's headers is unverified; if it does not, the first patch is silently misparsed or dropped after the success message. That is an assumption about mail-parser behaviour. (b) `SubmitRequest::Inject.raw` is a `String` and the CLI uses `read_to_string`, so any mbox with non-UTF-8 bytes, such as a Latin-1 diff, is refused at the CLI. The server ingest path (`ingestor::split_mbox`, `extract_message_id` via `from_utf8_lossy`, `parse_email(&[u8])`) is byte-oriented, so the String-only wire type and CLI read are the limiting factor. The shell re-encoding to `?` that the candidate describes happens before the CLI sees the bytes and cannot be fixed in this code. To confirm (a), feed a BOM-prefixed single-patch mbox to `/api/submit` and check the stored patchset. Fix: strip a leading U+FEFF, and on a UTF-8 error report the encoding and suggest `git format-patch --stdout` through a byte-safe path.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The only place mbox bytes are decoded; it neither strips a BOM nor accepts non-UTF-8 bytes, and the result goes into a String-typed Inject.raw.
A BOM before 'From ' makes the first separator line fail this check, so the envelope line stays inside the first message.

findings.problem: submit with no INPUT reads stdin whenever it is not a TTY
findings.explanation: Consequence: an unattended run of 'sashiko-cli submit' with no INPUT (cron, systemd, CI, a script launched with inherited stdin) does not use the documented HEAD default. With stdin on /dev/null or NUL, the CLI posts an empty mbox and the server rejects it. With an open stdin that never closes, the CLI hangs forever. Reachability: only submit with no INPUT and no --type, so it is an operator or script path, not a hot path. Empty-payload half is not silent: handle_submit in src/api.rs rejects it with 'if raw.trim().is_empty() { return Err(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST); }'. The CLI turns that into 'Submission failed (400 Bad Request): ' with an empty body, prints it and exits 1. That output does not say stdin was the problem, because the CLI never checks for empty content before posting. The server also has a second guard for non-mbox text (the 'From ' / 'Subject:' check). Hang half: 'std::io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut buffer)' is synchronous, unbounded and has no deadline. It sits in an async fn on the tokio main runtime. With a single task there is no other work to starve, so the worker-blocking concern is minor. The real effect is that the process waits indefinitely and buffers all of stdin in memory. Reading stdin when piped is documented in the help text. The defect is that the TTY check cannot tell 'a patch is being piped' from 'stdin is just not a terminal'. It overrides the 'Defaults to HEAD if in a git repo' branch in exactly the unattended cases. Platform: the same on Windows (a non-interactive PowerShell host or scheduled task has a non-terminal stdin) and on Linux. Fix: the CLI should refuse an empty stdin payload with a clear message, and ideally require an explicit '-' to read stdin.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Terminal detection decides the submission type for unattended runs and shadows the HEAD default.

locations.code_snippet: std::io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut buffer).context("Failed to read from stdin")?;
locations.why_this_location_matters: Blocking, unbounded read with no empty-content check before the POST.
Shows the server answer for an empty raw: 400 with no body, so the failure is loud but unexplained.

findings.problem: submit sends default repo path as a git remote URL, unresolved
findings.explanation: Consequence: 'sashiko-cli submit <sha>' and the Range form post a 'repo' string taken unchanged from --repo or from settings.git.repository_path. The server uses that string as a git remote URL. Reachability: every Remote and Range submit that does not pass an absolute, server-resolvable path. This is the default flow. Evidence: Settings.toml sets 'repository_path = "third_party/linux"', a relative path. The CLI sends it as SubmitRequest::Remote { sha, repo }. The api.rs handler forwards it as 'FetchRequest { repo_url: repo, commit_hash: sha }'. FetchAgent.ensure_remote runs 'git remote add <name> <url>' with 'current_dir(&self.repo_path)', and fetch_commits and fetch_all then run 'git fetch <remote>' in that same directory. The server's repo_path is that same 'third_party/linux'. A relative local-path remote is resolved against the cwd at fetch time, so the remote points at third_party/linux/third_party/linux. That path does not exist, the fetch fails, and the server emits Event::IngestionFailed. The user has already received 'Submission accepted' plus a placeholder 'Fetching ... from ...' patchset, so the failure shows up only later in the server log or patchset status. Other forms fail the same way. '~' is expanded only by shells (PowerShell 5.1 and cron do not expand it inside an argument like --repo=~/x), and git does not expand it in a remote URL. A relative --repo is resolved against the server's directory, not the user's cwd. A Windows path such as C:\src\linux, produced by to_string_lossy on a Windows desktop, means nothing to a Linux server. The CLI also loads Settings from its own cwd and environment, which can differ from the running server's config. The assumption is that the server runs with the repo's Settings.toml defaults. If its deployment uses an absolute repository_path and the CLI loads the same file, the default case works and only the --repo cases remain. --repo is documented only as 'Override repository path (defaults to settings)', which suggests a local path, while the server treats it as a remote URL or path on its own host. Fix: document --repo as a server-side URL or path, or canonicalize local paths (expand '~', make relative paths absolute) in the CLI, and make the server resolve the value against its own repo or reject it with a 400.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The path crosses the process and host boundary with no expansion or canonicalization.
The value is used verbatim as a remote URL inside the server's repo, so a relative path resolves against that repo.
The default sent by the CLI is relative, so it points at a nonexistent nested path from within that repo.

findings.problem: list panics slicing a multi-byte subject at byte 45
findings.explanation: Consequence: sashiko-cli list aborts with a panic instead of printing the table whenever one displayed row has a subject longer than 48 bytes whose byte 45 falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character. A single such row hides the whole page. Reachability: handle_list does `subject.len() > 48` and then `&subject[..45]`. Both use byte offsets, and str slicing panics off a char boundary. Subjects come from mailing-list mail through the server's PatchsetRow.subject, and non-ASCII text in subjects (names, CJK, accented characters) is routine. Any `sashiko-cli list` page containing such a patchset, in text format, triggers it; the default `list` is exactly this path. This was found while verifying H12's division by per_page: that division itself is safe against the real server (see dismissal), but the same function has this crash. It follows the error-handling guidance that `&s[..n]` panics inside a multi-byte character. It is not preexisting because the file is new in this commit. A fix is to truncate on chars, e.g. `subject.chars().take(45).collect::<String>()`, and to count chars rather than bytes for the length test.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Byte-index slice of a server-supplied, mail-derived string; panics when byte 45 is not a char boundary.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: handle_list divides by the server-returned per_page, which could panic with division by zero if per_page were 0.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: list_patchsets is the only sashiko route that builds PatchsetsResponse.
